# Azure Mastery

> Azure Mastery is an iOS and iPadOS app for Microsoft certification exam preparation (Azure, AI, Data, Security, Power Platform, and GitHub). It uses on-device CoreML to predict your exam score (Exam IQ), build adaptive study plans, and track knowledge decay before exam day. 12,200+ practice questions cover 30 Microsoft certification exams. The app runs 100% offline with no tracking and no data collection.

Publisher: Moonbeam Alpha Ltd
Platform: iOS 18+, iPadOS 18+
Pricing: Free to download, with optional in-app purchases for full per-exam question banks. No subscription required for core study features.
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6760594569
Last updated: 2026-08-09

## Primary pages

- [Home — Azure Mastery](https://azuremastery.app/): Product overview, feature list, screenshots, and App Store link. Canonical entry point.
- [All exam pages](https://azuremastery.app/exams/): Hub listing every covered exam by family with links to each practice page.
- [About Azure Mastery](https://azuremastery.app/about/): Who publishes the app, what it does, and how it's built.
- [How we write and verify practice questions](https://azuremastery.app/how-we-write-questions/): How questions are written against Microsoft's published skills outlines, checked on every change, and watched weekly for drift.
- [How Exam IQ predicts your score](https://azuremastery.app/how-exam-iq-works/): How the on-device Exam IQ engine predicts a certification exam score from your practice record with an on-device CoreML model.
- [Retired Microsoft exams and what replaced them](https://azuremastery.app/exams/retired/): The five retired exams (AI-900, AI-102, DP-100, AZ-204, AZ-500), when each retired, and its current successor exam.
- [Support](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/support.html): User support, contact, and FAQ.
- [Privacy Policy](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/privacy.html): Data handling — none collected; everything runs on-device.
- [Terms of Use](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/terms.html): Standard EULA for in-app purchases.

## Per-exam landing pages

Every exam covered by the app has a dedicated landing page describing the exam, the in-app question count, the official Microsoft Learn skills outline, a suggested study plan, and cert-specific FAQs. Question counts are extracted directly from the app's bundled question banks. Each page ships a single `@graph` JSON-LD block linking 6 entities (WebPage, BreadcrumbList, EducationalOccupationalCredential, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, HowTo) for AI/AEO discoverability. The first 5 below are the most heavily-trafficked Azure exams and ship the deepest per-domain breakdowns.

### Azure infrastructure & solutions (5)

- [AZ-900 — Microsoft Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-900/): 364 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration; most Fundamentals sittings contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count varies. Pass score 700/1000. Three domains: cloud concepts (25–30%), Azure architecture and services (35–40%), Azure management and governance (30–35%). Skills measured as of 20 July 2026.

- [AZ-104 — Microsoft Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-104/): 481 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier sysadmin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five domains: identities and governance (20–25%), storage (15–20%), compute (20–25%), virtual networking (15–20%), monitoring (10–15%). Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-305 — Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-305/): 399 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier solution architect cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions plus case studies. Four design domains: identity/governance/monitoring (25–30%), data storage (20–25%), business continuity (15–20%), infrastructure (30–35%). Recommended Associate prerequisite: AZ-104. Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-204 — Developing Solutions for Microsoft Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-204/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. **⚠ Microsoft retired AZ-204 on 31 July 2026** — it can no longer be scheduled; the current AI cloud developer route is AI-200. Five developer domains: compute (25–30%), storage (15–20%), security (15–20%), monitor/troubleshoot/optimize (5–10%), connect/consume services (20–25%). Heavy on SDK code samples in C#/Python/JavaScript. Skills outline updated 14 January 2026.

- [AZ-400 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-400/): 467 in-app practice questions (largest single-cert bank). Expert-tier DevOps cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five DevOps domains: process/communications (10–15%), source control (10–15%), build/release pipelines (50–55%), security/compliance (10–15%), instrumentation (5–10%). Required Associate prerequisite: AZ-104 or an active Azure Developer Associate credential earned via the retired AZ-204 route. Skills measured as of 27 July 2026.

- [AZ-500 — Microsoft Azure Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-500/): 346 in-app practice questions. **⚠ Microsoft retired AZ-500 on 31 August 2026** — it can no longer be scheduled; the successor is SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer). Associate-tier security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing identity and access (Entra, conditional access, PIM), securing networking (NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link, DDoS), securing compute/storage/databases, and managing security operations (Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Key Vault). Skills outline updated 22 January 2026.

- [AZ-700 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-700/): 569 in-app practice questions. Specialty-tier network engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing/implementing core networking (VNets, peering, hybrid), private access (Private Link, ExpressRoute, VPN), routing and load balancing (Application Gateway, Load Balancer, Front Door, Traffic Manager), and securing/monitoring networks. Skills measured as of 27 July 2026.

### AI, Machine Learning & Copilot Agents (11)

- [AI-900 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-900/): 340 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-900 on 30 June 2026 and replaced it with AI-901; AI-900 can no longer be scheduled.

- [AI-901 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-901/): 572 in-app practice questions. Current replacement for retired AI-900; the Fundamentals credential does not expire and local exam pricing varies. 45-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Two assessed areas: identify AI concepts and responsibilities (40–45%); implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%). Requires foundational cloud/Azure knowledge and understanding Python examples. English exam updated 15 April 2026.

- [AI-102 — Designing and Implementing a Microsoft Azure AI Solution (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-102/): 334 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-102 on 30 June 2026; the current role-based Azure AI apps and agents route is AI-103.

- [AI-103 — Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-103/): 557 in-app practice questions for the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential. 100-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/manage an Azure AI solution (25–30%), generative and agentic solutions (30–35%), computer vision (10–15%), text analysis (10–15%), and information extraction (10–15%). Requires Python and Microsoft Foundry experience. Skills measured as of 16 April 2026.

- [AI-200 — Azure AI Cloud Developer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-200/): 220 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier AI cloud developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing cloud-native AI applications, embedding LLMs into Azure-hosted apps, integrating with Azure AI Search and storage, and operationalising AI workloads. Study guide updated 5 May 2026.

- [AI-300 — Microsoft Azure ML Operations Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-300/): 362 in-app practice questions (covers the ML Operations Engineer role). Associate-tier cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing the ML lifecycle on Azure ML — model training pipelines, registries, deployment to managed and Kubernetes endpoints, monitoring drift, and responsible-AI evaluation in production. Study guide updated 26 July 2026.

- [AI-500 — Microsoft Multi-Agent AI Solutions Expert](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-500/): 452 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier cert, launched in beta in 2026. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Four domains: architect multi-agent solutions (15–20%), develop multi-agent solutions in Azure (30–35%), evaluate, optimize, and monitor multi-agent solutions (20–25%), and secure, govern, and deploy multi-agent solutions (20–25%). Covers Microsoft Foundry, the Microsoft Agent Framework, orchestration patterns, A2A and MCP protocols, agent observability, and Microsoft Entra Agent ID. Study guide updated 16 July 2026.

- [AB-410 — Microsoft Intelligent Applications Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-410/): 424 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert with a 120-minute assessment for makers who build AI-powered business solutions in Microsoft Power Platform using Copilot, natural-language prompts, and low-code tools. Three domains: create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%), create intelligent applications (25–30%), and build business application logic and automation (40–45%). Microsoft's study guide was last updated 15 May 2026. Successor route for makers who previously targeted PL-200 — Microsoft replaced course PL-200T00 with AB-410T00.

- [AB-620 — Microsoft AI Agent Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-620/): 387 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert focused on designing and building integrated AI solutions in Copilot Studio. Three domains: plan/configure agent solutions (30–35%), integrate/extend agents (40–45%), and test/manage agents (20–25%). Official study guide updated 21 April 2026.

- [AB-650 — Microsoft AI Services Administrator Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-650/): 506 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier admin cert, launched in beta in 2026. 120-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: configure and manage Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (20–25%), govern and secure Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (40–45%), and manage and secure AI services in Microsoft 365 (35–40%). For Microsoft 365 administrators taking on Copilot, agent governance with Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Agent ID, and Microsoft Purview data security for AI. Study guide updated 27 July 2026.

- [AB-731 — Microsoft AI Transformation Leader](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-731/): 335 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier leadership cert (no-code), does not expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration (65-min seat), 30–40 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%), identify benefits/capabilities of Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%), identify an implementation and adoption strategy (20–25%). For business decision-makers, programme leads, and AI champions — not builders. Study guide updated 22 July 2026.

- [AB-900 — Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-900/): 323 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration; most Fundamentals sittings contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count varies. Pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify core features/objects of Microsoft 365 (30–35%), data protection and governance for M365 and Copilot (35–40%), basic admin tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%). For IT admins deploying and governing Copilot. Skills measured as of 22 July 2026.

- [AB-100 — Microsoft Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-100/): 443 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier architect cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates architecting multi-agent enterprise solutions with the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework, Microsoft Agent Framework, MCP extensibility, Computer Use, agent feed, and DSPM for AI. Skills measured as of 22 July 2026.

### Data (5)

- [DP-900 — Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-900/): 346 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration; most Fundamentals sittings contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count varies. Pass score 700/1000. Validates core data concepts (relational vs non-relational, OLTP vs OLAP), relational data on Azure (Azure SQL family), non-relational data on Azure (Cosmos DB, blob/file/table), and analytics workloads (Synapse, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI fundamentals). Skills measured as of 21 July 2026.

- [DP-100 — Designing and Implementing a Data Science Solution on Azure (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-100/): 350 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired DP-100 on 1 June 2026; it can no longer be scheduled.

- [DP-300 — Administering Microsoft Azure SQL Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-300/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier database administrator cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/implement data platform resources (15–20%), implement secure environment (20–25%), monitor/configure/optimize (20–25%), automation (15–20%), HA/DR (20–25%). Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

- [DP-700 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-700/): 336 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Microsoft Fabric data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains each weighted 30–35%: implement and manage an analytics solution (Fabric workspaces, Git and deployment pipelines, OneLake security, orchestration), ingest and transform data (full/incremental loads, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks, PySpark, T-SQL, KQL, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, Eventstream and Spark Structured Streaming), and monitor and optimize an analytics solution (alerts, error resolution, Lakehouse/Warehouse/Spark tuning). Requires SQL, PySpark, or KQL. Skills outline updated 21 July 2026.

- [DP-750 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Azure Databricks](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-750/): 442 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Azure Databricks data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Four domains: set up and configure an Azure Databricks environment (15–20%), secure and govern Unity Catalog objects (15–20%), prepare and process data (30–35%), deploy and maintain data pipelines and workloads (30–35%). Covers compute selection, Unity Catalog objects and governance (grants, row/column security, ABAC, lineage, Delta Sharing), Delta modelling and Lakeflow/Auto Loader ingestion, Spark optimisation (OPTIMIZE, VACUUM), and CI/CD with Databricks Asset Bundles. Requires SQL and Python. Skills outline updated 11 March 2026.

- [DP-800 — Microsoft Certified: SQL AI Developer Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-800/): 393 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SQL developer cert focused on AI-enabled SQL workloads (exam title: "Developing AI-Enabled Database Solutions"), renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration (120-min seat), 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: design and develop database solutions (35–40%) — advanced T-SQL, JSON, regex, fuzzy matching, graph queries, AI-assisted dev; secure/optimize/deploy (35–40%); implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%) — embeddings, vector indexes, RAG with `sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint`. Skills outline published 12 March 2026.

### Security, Compliance & Identity (5)

- [SC-900 — Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-900/): 397 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration; most Fundamentals sittings contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count varies. Pass score 700/1000. Validates security, compliance, and identity concepts; Microsoft Entra ID capabilities; Microsoft Defender XDR security solutions; and Microsoft Purview compliance solutions. Skills measured as of 28 July 2026.

- [SC-100 — Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-100/): 452 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier cybersecurity architect cert (single exam earns the credential, with prerequisite Associate cert). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 120-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing Zero Trust strategy and architecture, evaluating governance/risk/compliance technical strategies, designing security for infrastructure, and designing security for data and applications. Skills measured as of 28 July 2026.

- [SC-200 — Microsoft Security Operations Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-200/): 374 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SOC analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates mitigating threats with Microsoft Defender XDR (Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, Cloud Apps), mitigating threats with Microsoft Sentinel (KQL, analytics rules, watchlists, hunting), and managing security operations across the Microsoft security stack. Skills measured as of 28 July 2026.

- [SC-300 — Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-300/): 428 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier identity admin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates implementing identities in Microsoft Entra ID, implementing authentication and access management (conditional access, MFA, PIM, passwordless), implementing access management for apps, and planning/implementing identity governance. Skills outline updated 27 April 2026.
- [SC-500 — Microsoft Cloud and AI Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-500/): 432 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cloud and AI security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. The current successor to retired AZ-500. Validates managing identity, access, and governance (Entra ID, PIM, Key Vault, Azure Policy, RBAC); securing storage, databases, and networking (Defender for Storage, Azure SQL, NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link); securing compute and AI workloads (Defender for Servers/Containers, plus securing AI — Entra Agent ID, Defender for AI, AI Gateway for Foundry, Purview DSPM for Copilot); and managing and monitoring security posture (Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Security Copilot). Study guide updated 13 May 2026.

### Power Platform (2)

- [PL-300 — Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-300/): 378 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier data analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates preparing data (Power Query M, data profiling), modelling data (star schemas, DAX measures, calculation groups, row-level security), visualising and analysing data (Power BI reports, dashboards, AI visuals), and deploying/maintaining assets (workspaces, deployment pipelines, refresh, sensitivity labels). Skills measured as of 20 April 2026.
- [PL-900 — Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-900/): 328 in-app practice questions. Fundamentals-tier low-code cert, never expires, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration; most Fundamentals sittings contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count varies. Pass score 700/1000. Validates the business value of Power Platform, managing the environment (Dataverse, security model, ALM pipelines), Power Apps (canvas, model-driven and code apps, plus AI-built apps), Power Automate (cloud and desktop flows), and building agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio (topics, knowledge sources, MCP tools, channels). Skills outline updated 24 July 2026.

### GitHub (2)
- [GH-300 — GitHub Copilot](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-300/): 356 in-app practice questions. Intermediate GitHub certification covering responsible AI use, Copilot features (IDE, Copilot CLI, Agent Mode, Edit Mode, MCP, Copilot Chat, code review, org-wide policies), Copilot data and architecture, prompt engineering and context crafting, developer productivity, and privacy, content exclusions, and safeguards. Skills measured as of 7 August 2026.
- [GH-900 — GitHub Foundations](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-900/): 347 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier GitHub certification covering Git and GitHub basics, working with repositories, collaboration (issues, pull requests, discussions), modern development practices (GitHub Actions, Codespaces, Copilot), project management, privacy/security/administration, and the GitHub community. Skills measured as of January 2026.

## Guides

Free long-form study guides — exam-neutral advice grounded in the official Microsoft Learn skills outlines. Every guide article includes FAQ structured data, and the ten how-to guides also include study-plan structured data. Index: [Azure certification guides](https://azuremastery.app/guides/).

- [Which Microsoft certification should you get first?](https://azuremastery.app/guides/which-azure-certification-first/): Decision guide mapping roles (IT ops, security, data, AI, business) to the right entry certification and its associate-level follow-on.
- [How to pass AZ-900 Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-900/): Study plan, domain breakdown, hardest topics, and what to do after passing.
- [How to pass AZ-104 Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-104/): Six-week study plan, domain weights, hardest topics (networking, RBAC), and exam-day tactics.
- [How to pass SC-900 Security Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-sc-900/): Security, compliance, and identity fundamentals prep with next steps into SC-500/SC-200.
- [How to pass DP-900 Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-dp-900/): Core data concepts, relational vs non-relational, analytics, and the data career path.
- [How to pass AI-901 AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-901/): The AI-900 successor — AI workloads, generative AI, responsible AI, and the AI-103 path.
- [How to pass AI-103 Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-103/): All five skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the Foundry-based AI apps and agents exam.
- [How to pass AB-620 Copilot Studio AI Agent Builder](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ab-620/): All three skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the low-code Copilot Studio agent exam.
- [How to pass AB-100 Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ab-100/): All three skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the multi-agent architecture exam.
- [How to pass SC-500 Cloud and AI Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-sc-500/): All four skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for AZ-500's successor.
- [How to pass AI-200 Azure AI Cloud Developer](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-200/): All four skills domains and weights, a six-week study plan, and exam-day tactics for the AI cloud back-end exam.
- [AZ-900 vs AZ-104](https://azuremastery.app/guides/az-900-vs-az-104/): Which Azure certification fits, whether you need both, and in what order.
- [SC-900 vs AZ-900](https://azuremastery.app/guides/sc-900-vs-az-900/): Security-first or cloud-first — how the two fundamentals exams differ and which to sit first.
- [AB-620 vs AB-410](https://azuremastery.app/guides/ab-620-vs-ab-410/): Copilot Studio agent builder or intelligent-app builder — credential, domains, exam format, and which to build first.
- [AI-103 vs AI-200](https://azuremastery.app/guides/ai-103-vs-ai-200/): AI apps and agents or AI cloud developer — credential, domains, exam format, and which layer to sit first.
- [SC-500 vs AZ-500](https://azuremastery.app/guides/sc-500-vs-az-500/): What changed when Microsoft retired AZ-500, how SC-500 compares, and what carries over if you already hold AZ-500.

## Core capabilities

- **Exam IQ**: On-device CoreML model that predicts your exam-day score with a confidence range from your practice record (accuracy by domain, coverage, mastery, consistency, recency).
- **Adaptive study plans**: The app picks your next session — weak-spot drills, knowledge-decay refreshes, mock exams — based on your current ability estimate per domain.
- **Aura first-week guidance**: Aura suggests a next step based on the learner's progress throughout the first week. After each session, a short recap shows what improved and what needs more practice.
- **Exam simulator**: Full-length, timed practice tests using blueprint-weighted question sets; Microsoft's live interface and exact item mix may differ.
- **Knowledge decay tracking**: Spaced-repetition signals flag topics where your retention has dropped before exam day, with targeted refresher sessions.
- **Question types**: Nine interactive formats for exam-style rehearsal, including multiple choice, multi-select, drag-and-drop ordering, hotspot, and case studies.
- **Answer Coach**: See why the answer is correct and, where available, why each option is right or wrong. Review explanations after each question or at the end of a practice test, then return to missed answers and saved session notes. Written guidance is always available. On supported devices, optional AI can reword a note on the device after checking it against that guidance.
- **Offline-first**: Works fully without a network. No telemetry, no analytics on user behavior, no account required.
- **Apple ecosystem**: Native SwiftUI on iPhone and iPad; Live Activities for active study sessions; Apple Watch glance for streaks and XP.

## Differentiation

Azure Mastery is built for serious certification candidates who want to know *when they're ready* rather than just drilling questions. It is differentiated from generic flashcard apps by:

1. ML score prediction calibrated to Microsoft's pass thresholds, not a raw % correct.
2. Per-domain ability estimation — you see exactly which of an exam's domains is dragging your predicted score down.
3. Knowledge decay alerts so you don't lose old material while learning new domains.
4. Privacy-first computation — Exam IQ, Answer Coach, and study-plan generation run on-device; optional sync uses the learner's private iCloud account.

## /exams/ab-100/ — AB-100 Practice Questions — 443 Qs for AI Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Plan AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Design AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Deploy AI-powered business solutions (40–45%)
Q: How much does the AB-100 exam cost?
A: The AB-100 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; pricing varies by region). As an Expert-tier exam, AB-100 is rarely included in free-voucher promotions — if one appears around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, it's worth grabbing. Renewal itself stays free.
Q: Does the AB-100 certification expire?
A: Yes. Like Microsoft's other role-based certifications, AB-100 expires annually, with a free, short online renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn available in the six-month window before expiry — scoped to recent skills-outline updates. AB-900, the Fundamentals-tier exam, doesn't expire.
Q: What is the AB-100 retake policy if I fail?
A: Given how broad AB-100's syllabus is, treat a fail as a signal to target the weakest domain rather than rebook immediately. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months, each needing a fresh voucher.
Q: What does the AB-100 exam format look like?
A: AB-100 runs as a 100-minute session (120 minutes with seat time) of 40–60 questions, online or at a test centre, scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. Azure Mastery's bank leans heavier on multi-paragraph scenarios than the associate-level agent exams, so you read a business constraint before picking the architecture that fits it.
Q: How long should I study for AB-100?
A: Eight to twelve weeks if you already have hands-on time with at least one of Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, or Dynamics 365 Copilot. Give it three to four months if multi-agent orchestration is genuinely new — AB-100 expects you to design end-to-end solutions rather than describe the individual pieces.
Q: AB-100 vs AB-620 — which agent cert should I take?
A: AB-620 is for makers who build agents in Copilot Studio. AB-100 is for architects who choose the platform, governance, lifecycle management, and business case across Copilot Studio, Foundry, and Dynamics 365. Start with building agents, then move to AB-100 when your work includes those wider architecture decisions.
Q: AB-100 vs AI-103 vs AB-620 — how do the roles differ?
A: AI-103 is the code-first developer path (Python, Foundry). AB-620 is the Copilot Studio builder path (low-code agents). AB-100 sits above both as the architecture credential spanning every Microsoft AI surface. Get comfortable with an implementation credential before attempting the architecture-level exam.
Q: Do I need prerequisites before attempting AB-100?
A: Not formally, but AB-100 assumes it. Microsoft expects candidates to already hold AI-901-level knowledge, plus working experience with at least one of AI-102, AI-103, PL-200, PL-300, PL-400, PL-500, or AB-620. AB-100 tests architectural decisions across platforms you're assumed to already know individually — it isn't where most candidates start their Microsoft AI journey.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-100 prep?
A: The app is free to download with a free allowance of AB-100 questions. The full 443-question AB-100 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AB-100 practice work offline?
A: Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so a flight or offline commute won't interrupt your study streak. No account is required, and your data stays on-device unless you turn on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-410/ — AB-410 Practice Questions — 424 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Create intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Build business application logic and automation (40–45%)
Q: Is there a formal prerequisite for AB-410?
A: No exam gates AB-410 directly. Microsoft treats it as the successor to PL-200, and the PL-200T00 course has been replaced by AB-410T00, but you can book AB-410 without sitting anything first. If Power Platform concepts are new to you, PL-900 is a sensible primer.
Q: What does the AB-410 exam format actually look like?
A: AB-410 sits in Microsoft's general 40–60 question range, with exact formats varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank leans on single-answer and scenario items, with multi-select, drag-to-match, dropdown, hot-area, and case-study questions rounding things out — all original practice content.
Q: AB-410 vs AB-620 — which Power Platform builder credential fits?
A: Both sit on opposite sides of one solution. AB-410 builds the application — Dataverse tables, the app itself, the cloud flow — that consumes an agent. AB-620 builds that agent inside Copilot Studio: its topics, knowledge sources, and extensions.
Q: Does AB-410 expect me to build the Copilot Studio agent itself?
A: No — that's AB-620 territory. AB-410 tests the maker side: a canvas app that can spin up an agent, an existing agent consumed inside a model-driven app, and AI Hub prompts wired into apps and flows. Designing conversation topics belongs to the other exam.
Q: What does the AB-410 exam fee cover?
A: AB-410 costs USD $165 in the United States, though Microsoft adjusts pricing by country, so check the figure at booking. That fee covers one proctored attempt. The Associate certification it unlocks then needs renewing every year, and that renewal is free.
Q: I didn't pass AB-410 — how soon can I try again?
A: Each AB-410 retake needs its own voucher, and the wait depends on your attempt number. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: Is the AB-410 credential still valid after a year?
A: Associate certifications including AB-410 expire annually. Microsoft renews them through a short, unproctored assessment on Microsoft Learn, open during the six-month window before expiry — shorter than the original exam, not a repeat of it. Fundamentals certs such as AZ-900 don't expire at all.
Q: How long should I spend preparing for AB-410?
A: Four to eight weeks is typical if you already build apps, flows, and Dataverse tables day to day. Give yourself the longer end if Power Fx, prompt columns, or AI Hub are unfamiliar — the logic domain alone carries close to half the exam.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AB-410 content before paying?
A: The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AB-410 questions to try every feature first. The full bank of 424 AB-410 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-410 practice hold up on a train with no signal?
A: Yes — question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction run entirely on-device, so a dead connection costs you nothing. Starting needs no account, and your study data stays on your phone unless you switch on optional iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-620/ — AB-620 Practice Questions — 387 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Plan and configure agent solutions (30–35%)
  - Integrate and extend agents in Copilot Studio (40–45%)
  - Test and manage agents (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AB-620 exam cost?
A: The AB-620 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; pricing varies by region). Watch for occasional free-voucher promotions around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite — Microsoft doesn't run them year-round. Renewal itself is free.
Q: Does the AB-620 certification expire?
A: Yes — AB-620 expires annually like every Microsoft Associate certification. Renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six-month window before expiry and scoped to recent skills-outline updates. (Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.)
Q: What is the AB-620 retake policy if I fail?
A: Retake timing scales up with each failed attempt, and every attempt needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: What does the AB-620 exam format look like?
A: AB-620 runs as a 100-minute session (120 minutes with seat time) of 40–60 questions, taken online with a proctor or at a test centre, and scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. Azure Mastery's bank includes single-answer, multi-select, yes/no, and matching items, so it's not straight recall.
Q: How long should I study for AB-620?
A: Four to eight weeks if you already build with Copilot Studio or the wider Power Platform; longer if Power Fx, Dataverse, MCP, or agent lifecycle management are unfamiliar. The exam leans heavily on the Integrate and extend domain (40–45%), so prioritise hands-on time there.
Q: AB-620 vs AI-103 — different agent roles?
A: Different platforms for different builders. AB-620 covers Microsoft Copilot Studio, a low-code environment for topics, generative answers, and Power Platform integrations. AI-103 covers Microsoft Foundry, a code-first platform for Python-based agents and orchestration.
Q: AB-620 vs AI-901 — which should I take first?
A: Take AI-901 first if AI concepts are genuinely new to you — it's the Fundamentals exam and assumes no build experience. AB-620 is role-based and assumes you can already navigate Copilot Studio, Dataverse, and Power Platform environments.
Q: Do I need a Copilot Studio licence to prepare for AB-620?
A: Not to use Azure Mastery, but hands-on practice matters more for AB-620 than for most exams. Microsoft offers trial access to Copilot Studio — check the current terms on Microsoft Learn — and building topics, agent flows, and knowledge-source connections there pairs well with Azure Mastery's scenario questions, rather than relying on question practice alone.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-620 prep?
A: The app is free to download with a free allowance of AB-620 questions. The full 387-question AB-620 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AB-620 practice work offline?
A: Yes. The whole study loop, from answering questions to the readiness prediction, runs on the phone, so a flight or a signal-free commute is still study time. There is no account to create, and your progress stays on the device unless you switch on private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-650/ — AB-650 Practice Questions — 506 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Configure and manage Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (20–25%)
  - Govern and secure Microsoft 365 tenants and workloads (40–45%)
  - Manage and secure AI services in Microsoft 365 (35–40%)
Q: How much does the AB-650 exam cost?
A: Microsoft prices AB-650 by region and hasn't published a flat beta fee — check the official exam page when you register. During the beta, Microsoft sometimes opens a discounted registration window announced on the Learn blog. Renewal afterwards is a free annual online assessment.
Q: Does the AB-650 certification expire?
A: Yes. Associate certifications including AB-650 expire annually, renewed free through a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before expiry. Fundamentals certifications such as AB-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the AB-650 retake policy if I fail?
A: AB-650's beta status changes this for now. During the beta: you can take the exam only once. If you do not pass, you can retake it after the exam becomes generally available; then the standard 24-hour first-retake and 14-day later-retake waits apply. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months, each needing its own voucher.
Q: How long should I study for AB-650?
A: Four to eight weeks is typical if you already administer Microsoft 365 tenants and Microsoft Entra ID. Spend longer if Purview, Conditional Access, Agent 365, or Microsoft Entra Agent ID are unfamiliar. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge is the better signal for when to book.
Q: AB-650 vs AB-620 — administer or build?
A: Different roles over the same agent estate. AB-620 is the maker-role exam for designing agents inside Copilot Studio. AB-650 is the administrator-role exam: governing whatever agents your organisation ends up with — licensing, identity, Defender, Purview, and Agent 365 monitoring.
Q: AB-650 vs AB-900 — do I need the fundamentals exam first?
A: AB-900 stays conceptual — what Copilot and agent administration are for. AB-650 expects you to actually configure tenant settings, identity policies, and governance controls, and defend the trade-offs between similar options. AB-900 isn't a formal prerequisite, but it's a solid foundation.
Q: AB-650 vs SC-300 — how much identity overlap is there?
A: SC-300 goes far deeper into Microsoft Entra identity architecture — hybrid identity, application integration, identity governance. AB-650 covers the identity surface an administrator actually touches day to day, plus the newer agent identity model that SC-300 doesn't cover.
Q: What does the AB-650 exam format actually look like?
A: AB-650 follows Microsoft's general 40–60 question range, varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank weights single-answer and scenario items most heavily, with multi-select, drag-to-match, dropdown, hot-area, and case-study questions layered in — all original practice content.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AB-650 content before paying?
A: The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AB-650 questions to try every feature first. The full bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-650 practice work without a connection?
A: Yes — practice, scoring, and the Exam IQ prediction happen entirely on-device, so a commute with no signal works the same as being online. Nothing to sign up for; iCloud sync is available if you want it.

## /exams/ab-731/ — AB-731 Practice Questions — 335 Qs for AI Leadership (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%)
  - Identify benefits, capabilities, and opportunities for Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%)
  - Identify an implementation and adoption strategy for Microsoft's AI apps and services (20–25%)
Q: Do I need any coding background before AB-731?
A: No. AB-731 is a no-code, leadership-level exam — you're not expected to build an agent or write Power Fx. Microsoft expects working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and a sense of how generative AI differs from earlier AI. If that's new, AI-901 is a reasonable warm-up, though not a formal prerequisite.
Q: What does the AB-731 exam format actually look like?
A: AB-731's published guidance is 30–40 questions in mixed formats over a 45-minute session. Azure Mastery's bank weights single-answer and scenario items most heavily, with multi-select, drag-to-match, and case-study questions layered in — all original practice content.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-620 — which is right for me?
A: Different jobs. AB-731 is the leadership credential for decision-makers framing ROI, choosing build/buy/extend, and running adoption programmes. AB-620 is the maker credential for low-code builders shipping agents in Copilot Studio. Pick AB-731 to lead change, AB-620 to build.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-900 — what's the difference?
A: Different audiences. AB-900 is the IT admin's Fundamentals exam — admin centres, governance, licensing, agent approval flows. AB-731 is the business leader's exam — ROI, adoption strategy, responsible AI, and build/buy/extend decisions. Programme leads sometimes take both.
Q: AB-731 vs AI-901 — business leader or technical fundamentals?
A: Different audiences. AB-731 is a no-code, Beginner-tier exam for decision-makers spotting AI opportunities and driving adoption. AI-901 expects technical grounding — Python, Azure resources, Foundry — for people starting a technical AI career. A programme lead wants AB-731; an engineer wants AI-901.
Q: What does the AB-731 exam fee cover?
A: AB-731 is Beginner-tier: the voucher is USD $99 in the US, around £77 in the UK. Microsoft occasionally offers free vouchers via Build, Ignite, or virtual training events, so check your Learn profile before booking. Pricing varies by region.
Q: What is the AB-731 retake policy if I fail?
A: Each retake needs its own voucher, and the wait depends on your attempt number. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: How long should I study for AB-731?
A: Most decision-makers pass after three to five weeks of focused study, assuming familiarity with Microsoft 365 and basic generative-AI concepts. You don't need to build agents, but you do need to articulate ROI, licensing, and adoption frameworks. Don't book until the readiness gauge shows 720 or higher.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AB-731 content before paying?
A: The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AB-731 questions to try every feature first. The full bank of 335 AB-731 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-731 practice work offline?
A: Yes — every part of practice runs locally: questions, scoring, and the readiness read. A flight or a signal-free commute doesn't interrupt a session. No account is needed, and data stays on your device until you turn on optional iCloud sync.

## /exams/ab-900/ — AB-900 Practice Questions — 323 Qs for Copilot Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Identify the core features and objects of Microsoft 365 services (30–35%)
  - Understand data protection and governance tasks for Microsoft 365 and Copilot (35–40%)
  - Perform basic administrative tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%)
Q: Which admin centre owns a given object — is that a recurring AB-900 trap?
A: Yes. AB-900 often gives an object, a mailbox setting, a Teams policy, a SharePoint site, and expects you to know which admin centre actually owns it, rather than treating the centres as interchangeable. Answer Coach names the specific centre a wrong pick would have sent you to instead.
Q: AB-900 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: Different scopes. SC-900 is the broad Microsoft security overview: Entra, Defender, Purview, identity. AB-900 is narrower and practical, focused on M365 Copilot administration, with Purview coverage scoped to the Copilot threat surface. Passed SC-900 already? AB-900 feels like an extension. New to both? Start with AB-900 if your role is Copilot-focused.
Q: What question formats should I expect on AB-900?
A: Most Microsoft Fundamentals exams contain 35–50 questions, but the exact count and formats vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's original practice bank includes single-select, scenario, yes/no, multi-select, drag-to-match, hot-area, drag-and-drop, dropdown, and case-study interactions.
Q: What's the AB-900 exam fee, and does it vary by region?
A: The listed US price is USD $99, while regional pricing and promotions can change. Check Microsoft's exam page and current offers before booking. Fundamentals certifications never expire, so there's no annual renewal cost.
Q: Once earned, does an AB-900 credential ever lapse?
A: No. AB-900, like other Microsoft Fundamentals certifications (AZ-900, AI-901, SC-900, DP-900), never expires once earned. Associate and Specialty certifications differ: those require annual renewal on Microsoft Learn.
Q: DSPM for AI vs standard DLP — how does AB-900 tell them apart?
A: AB-900 tests whether you know DSPM for AI is scoped to Copilot and agent interactions, flagging oversharing and exposure risk in prompts and grounding data, while standard DLP governs data movement across email, Teams, and file storage generally. Picking the wrong one is the exact mix-up Answer Coach catches.
Q: I failed AB-900 — how soon can I book a retake?
A: The wait before your first retake is 24 hours. First retake: 24-hour wait. Second and third retakes: 14-day wait each. Microsoft caps you at five attempts within any rolling 12-month period, a voucher required each time.
Q: AB-900 vs AB-620 — what's the difference?
A: Different jobs. AB-900 is the Fundamentals-tier admin cert: identifying M365 admin-centre objects, Purview surfaces, and Copilot administration controls. AB-620 (AI Agent Builder) is the Associate-tier maker cert: building agents in Copilot Studio with topics and knowledge sources. AB-900 administers; AB-620 builds. Many admins take both.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AB-900 bank before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download with a free allowance of AB-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full 323-question bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Can I revise AB-900 offline?
A: Yes. Nothing in the study loop needs a connection: practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all happen on-device. No account is needed, and your data only leaves the device if you opt into private iCloud sync.

## /exams/ai-102/ — AI-102 Retired Exam & AI-103 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Plan and manage an Azure AI solution (20–25%)
  - Implement generative AI solutions (15–20%)
  - Implement an agentic solution (5–10%)
  - Implement computer vision solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement natural language processing solutions (15–20%)
  - Implement knowledge mining and information extraction solutions (15–20%)
Q: Can I still take the AI-102 exam?
A: No. Microsoft retired AI-102 and the Azure AI Engineer Associate certification on 30 June 2026. The exam can no longer be scheduled.
Q: What replaced AI-102?
A: AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. It leads to the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential and assesses Python, Microsoft Foundry, generative and agentic solutions, vision, text analysis, and information extraction.
Q: What happens if I already earned Azure AI Engineer Associate?
A: A certification earned before retirement remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-102 and its renewal assessment are retired, so the exam cannot be retaken or newly earned.
Q: Are AI-102 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for Azure AI services, generative AI, vision, language, search, and document intelligence. New candidates should study the current AI-103 outline and use its exam-specific bank.
Q: What is the current path after AI-102 retirement?
A: AI-901 is the current Azure AI Fundamentals exam, and AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. AI-102 content remains useful as historical reference, but new candidates should use the AI-901 and AI-103 outlines rather than planning an AI-102 certification path.
Q: What replaced the retired AI-102 and DP-100 routes?
A: Microsoft replaced the retired AI-102 route with AI-103 for Azure AI apps and agents, and identifies AI-300 as the replacement for the retired DP-100 data-science route. AI-103 focuses on application and agent development; AI-300 focuses on operationalizing machine learning and generative AI systems.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-102 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-102 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 334 AI-102 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AI-102 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-102 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/ai-103/ — AI-103 Practice Questions — 557 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06

  - Implement generative AI and agentic solutions (30–35%)
  - Implement computer vision solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement text analysis solutions (10–15%)
  - Implement information extraction solutions (10–15%)
Q: How much does the AI-103 exam cost?
A: The AI-103 voucher costs USD $165 in the United States (around £128 in the UK; regional pricing varies). Because AI-103 is a role-based Associate exam rather than a Fundamentals-tier one, Microsoft rarely bundles it into free promotional vouchers — watch for occasional offers around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite instead. Renewal itself is free.
Q: Does the AI-103 certification expire?
A: Yes — like every Microsoft Associate certification, AI-103 expires annually. Renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six-month window before expiry and scoped to recent skills-outline updates. AI-901, the Fundamentals-tier exam, doesn't expire — only role-based certifications like AI-103 do.
Q: What is the AI-103 retake policy if I fail?
A: How much time you need before retaking AI-103 depends on your attempt number; every attempt needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: What does the AI-103 exam format look like?
A: AI-103 runs as a 100-minute session (120 minutes with seat time) of 40–60 questions, taken online with a proctor or at a test centre, and scored out of 1000 with a 700 pass mark. Azure Mastery's bank practises the same formats: multiple choice, multi-select, ordering, matching, and case studies.
Q: How long should I study for AI-103?
A: Plan for several weeks of focused study if you already write Python and know Azure AI services; extend that if Foundry, agents, or multimodal AI are new to you. The exam spans five distinct domains, so breadth matters as much as depth. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge shows when you've closed the gap.
Q: AI-103 vs AI-102 — different roles?
A: AI-102 retired on 30 June 2026. AI-103 replaced it as the current Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate exam, a genuinely new outline that reflects how far the underlying platform has shifted toward Microsoft Foundry, agentic patterns, and multimodal content since AI-102.
Q: AI-103 vs AI-901 — which should I take first?
A: Take AI-901 first if generative AI and Microsoft Foundry are unfamiliar concepts — it's the Fundamentals exam and assumes no coding. AI-103 assumes you can already write Python and expects hands-on familiarity with Foundry projects, agent tools, retrieval, and evaluation. Candidates with existing development experience sometimes skip AI-901 and go straight to AI-103.
Q: Do I need real Foundry or Python experience before I start?
A: Not to begin studying, but AI-103 is written for candidates who already develop with Python and have touched Azure services — it isn't an intro-to-AI exam. If you're newer to development, working through Microsoft Foundry's own quickstarts alongside Azure Mastery's practice questions will close that gap faster than question practice alone.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-103 prep?
A: The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AI-103 questions to try Answer Coach, the readiness gauge, and the adaptive plan before you commit. The full 557-question AI-103 bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription or lifetime upgrade unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does AI-103 practice work offline?

## /exams/ai-200/ — AI-200 Practice Questions — 220 Qs for AI Developer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Develop containerized solutions on Azure (20–25%)
  - Develop AI solutions by using Azure data management services (25–30%)
  - Connect to and consume Azure services (20–25%)
  - Secure, monitor, and troubleshoot Azure solutions (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AI-200 exam cost?
A: The AI-200 voucher is USD $165 in the United States, around £128 in the UK; regional pricing varies. Watch for free-voucher promotions around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite. Renewal is free, but it's an annual Associate certification, so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AI-200 certification expire?
A: Yes. The AI-200 Associate credential has one-year validity. During its final six months, you can extend it free by completing the current online renewal assessment in Microsoft Learn; Microsoft doesn't publish a fixed item count. Fundamentals credentials such as AZ-900 do not have this requirement.
Q: What is the AI-200 retake policy if I fail?
A: Waiting times step up after each fail, and every attempt needs a fresh voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: How long should I study for AI-200?
A: Allow four to eight weeks of focused study if you already develop on Azure. Spend longer if Python, Azure SDKs, containerized applications, Cosmos DB or PostgreSQL vector search, messaging, or KQL-based troubleshooting are new to you. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule the exam.
Q: What prior experience does AI-200 assume?
A: AI-200 assumes you already work across the AI-solution lifecycle on Azure — implementation, deployment, security, monitoring — with practical Python, SDK, and container experience. It expects you to already know your way around Azure data services, not learn them from the guide alone. Budget extra time if containers or vector databases are new.
Q: AI-200 vs AI-103 — different roles?
A: Different emphases. AI-200 validates back-end Azure development for AI solutions, including containers, data services, messaging, security, monitoring, and troubleshooting. AI-103 focuses on developing AI apps and agents with Python and Microsoft Foundry. AI-200 is cloud-platform and service integration; AI-103 is model, agent, retrieval, and AI-application implementation.
Q: AI-200 vs AI-300 — which next?
A: AI-200 first. It's the AI Cloud Developer cert, building the platform AI workloads run on. AI-300 is the ML Operations Engineer cert, running ML and generative-AI systems in production. AI-200 sits upstream of AI-300 in most roles.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-200 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-200 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 220 AI-200 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AI-200 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Everything AI-200 practice needs, from scoring to the readiness prediction, lives on the phone, so a flight or a dead spot changes nothing. There is no account to make, and your history only leaves the device if you turn on private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-200 practice test mode?
A: Yes. Exam Simulator runs a timed, blueprint-weighted AI-200 session built from the app's own questions, with the clock running and no jumping back to review. It is original practice content, so treat it as rehearsal for the pressure rather than a copy of Microsoft's paper.

## /exams/ai-900/ — AI-900 Retired Exam & AI-901 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Describe Artificial Intelligence workloads and considerations (15–20%)
  - Describe fundamental principles of machine learning on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of computer vision workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of Natural Language Processing (NLP) workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of generative AI workloads on Azure (20–25%)
Q: Can I still take the AI-900 exam?
A: No. Microsoft retired AI-900 on 30 June 2026, so it can no longer be scheduled. AI-901 is now the exam route to the Azure AI Fundamentals credential.
Q: What replaced AI-900?
A: AI-901 replaced AI-900 on 1 July 2026. It remains the route to Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals and adds a more implementation-oriented focus on Microsoft Foundry and Python examples.
Q: What happens if I already passed AI-900?
A: An Azure AI Fundamentals credential earned through AI-900 remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-900 itself is retired and cannot be retaken.
Q: Are AI-900 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for core AI, machine-learning, vision, language, and responsible-AI concepts. New candidates should study the current AI-901 outline and use the AI-901 bank for exam readiness.
Q: AI-900 vs AI-102 — which should I take first?
A: AI-900 first, unless you already build AI applications professionally. AI-900 is the conceptual map: it teaches you the vocabulary (image classification vs object detection, key phrase extraction vs entity recognition, regression vs classification, the Foundry model catalog) without expecting you to write code. AI-102 is the role-based Associate exam — it expects hands-on Python, REST API calls against Azure AI services, and prompt-engineering against Azure OpenAI. Most candidates pass AI-900 in a few weeks, then spend two to three months on AI-102.
Q: Is AI-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — that's a large part of the audience. Microsoft positions AI-900 for both technical and non-technical candidates: solution consultants, sales engineers, technical PMs, business stakeholders evaluating Azure AI procurement, and anyone wanting a credible answer to "which Azure AI service should we use for this?" The exam doesn't ask you to write Python. It asks you to recognise scenarios — "which Azure AI service is best suited for redacting PII from a document?" or "which guiding principle of responsible AI applies here?" — and pick the correct option.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AI-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AI-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 340 AI-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AI-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study on a flight or a commute with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AI-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes — timed practice sessions use original, blueprint-aligned questions, published timing guidance, and supported interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

Most architects hold both — one proves you've done the work, the other that you can design it.

  - Design data storage solutions (20–25%)
  - Design business continuity solutions (15–20%)

Q: Do I need AZ-104 before AZ-305?
A: Not to book it — Microsoft lets anyone sit AZ-305 directly. But the Solutions Architect Expert credential is only awarded once you also hold Azure Administrator Associate, earned through AZ-104. Pass AZ-305 first and you're just waiting on AZ-104 to unlock it. AZ-204 isn't an accepted alternative.
Q: What does the AZ-305 exam format actually look like?
A: Microsoft's general guidance is 40–60 questions plus case studies, with formats varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank weights single-answer, scenario-based, and multi-select items heaviest, then adds case-study sets, drag-and-drop, and hotspot questions — all original practice content, not a copy of Microsoft's live item mix.
Q: Why does AZ-305 feel harder than AZ-104 even with the same pass mark?
A: AZ-104 mostly checks whether you can configure a service; AZ-305 gives you a business constraint and asks which combination of services satisfies it, with rarely one "correct config" to recall. That judgement style takes longer to internalise, which is why AZ-305 has a higher first-attempt fail rate.
Q: Which AZ-305 domain catches candidates most off guard?
A: Business continuity, despite being the smallest domain by weight. Candidates who've only configured single VMs or databases under-prepare for scenarios mixing backup, disaster recovery, and high-availability requirements across compute, relational data, and unstructured data at once.
Q: What's the current AZ-305 exam voucher price?

Q: Does the Solutions Architect Expert badge need renewing?
A: Yes. Expert certifications including Azure Solutions Architect Expert expire annually. Renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within six months of your expiry date, targeting recent outline updates.
Q: I didn't pass AZ-305 — how soon can I try again?
A: Not immediately, and each sitting needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: Realistically, how many weeks does AZ-305 prep take?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks of focused study, even after passing AZ-104. AZ-305 tests judgement more than recall — you're given a scenario and asked which services satisfy it. Don't book until the readiness gauge holds around 730 or higher; AZ-305 is unforgiving of borderline scores.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's AZ-305 content before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AZ-305 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 399 AZ-305 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.

A: AZ-700 follows Microsoft's general 40–60 question guidance, with formats varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank weights single-answer and scenario-based items heaviest, then adds multi-select, hotspot, and linked case-study questions — every one original, never a copy of Microsoft's live item mix.
Q: AZ-700 vs AZ-104 — should I do AZ-104 first?
A: Microsoft strongly recommends it, and it shows. AZ-700 assumes you already know how Azure compute, storage, and the basic VNet model work day-to-day. If you've never deployed a VM with a public IP or set up a basic NSG, take AZ-104 first. Working network engineers can often skip straight in.
Q: What's the current AZ-700 voucher price?
A: The AZ-700 voucher is USD $165 in the US, or around £128 in the UK — pricing varies by region. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions around Build or Ignite. AZ-700 also needs annual renewal, so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does AZ-700 overlap with cloud security certs like SC-500?
A: A little, but the roles differ. AZ-700 treats network security (Firewall, NSGs, WAF) as one domain among five. SC-500 applies security controls across an entire cloud and AI estate, well beyond networking. Take AZ-700 for network engineering depth; add SC-500 for end-to-end cloud security.
Q: Does the AZ-700 badge need renewing every year?
A: Yes. Associate certifications including AZ-700 expire annually. Renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within six months of your expiry date. Fundamentals certs like AZ-900 are different — those never expire.
Q: Do I need a home lab to pass AZ-700?
A: Hands-on time helps more here than on most Associate exams, since AZ-700 is a design-and-build exam, not pure recall. A free-tier subscription is enough to build a hub-and-spoke topology, a site-to-site VPN, and an Application Gateway deployment. Azure Mastery's scenarios cover the harder-to-lab decisions too.
Q: If I don't pass AZ-700, when can I try again?
A: Not immediately, and each attempt needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: How many weeks of AZ-700 prep is realistic?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with prior Azure networking experience. Build and troubleshoot virtual networks, hybrid connectivity, routing, private access, application delivery, and network security in a lab. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're exam-ready.
Q: Can I test-drive Azure Mastery's AZ-700 content for free?
A: Yes. The app is free to download, with a free allowance of AZ-700 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 569 AZ-700 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.

## /exams/az-900/ — AZ-900 Practice Questions — 364 Qs for Fundamentals (2026)

Q: Does the AZ-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, MS-900, and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. (This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as AZ-104 or AZ-305, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.)
Q: What is the AZ-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: Retake waits get longer the more times you've failed, and every attempt needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If cloud computing is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you're at exam-ready — don't book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: AZ-900 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AZ-900 first, almost always. AZ-900 is designed as the on-ramp to AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator). It takes a few weeks to prepare for and doesn't expire; AZ-104 takes two to three months and requires hands-on PowerShell and CLI knowledge. Most people pass AZ-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.
Q: Is AZ-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes — that's exactly who it's designed for. Account managers, sales engineers, and finance partners sit AZ-900 to qualify for Microsoft Partner Network roles. It doesn't expect a PowerShell script, just an ability to explain region pairs, shared responsibility, and when hybrid cloud fits.
Q: What prerequisites does AZ-900 assume?
A: AZ-900 has no formal prerequisites — Microsoft designed it as the common entry point into Azure. Some IT background makes the material quicker to absorb, since you already have an environment to map its concepts onto. Coming from a fully non-technical background stretches the usual one-to-two-week estimate.

Q: Is there an AZ-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes. The simulator gives you a 45-minute, three-domain AZ-900 run built from the app's own questions, weighted the way Microsoft publishes the outline. Use it to practise pacing; the live exam's interface and mix are Microsoft's.

## /exams/dp-300/ — DP-300 Practice Questions — 405 Qs for Database Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Plan and implement data platform resources (15–20%)
  - Implement a secure environment (20–25%)
  - Monitor, configure, and optimize database resources (20–25%)
  - Configure and manage automation of tasks (15–20%)
  - Plan and configure a high availability and disaster recovery (HA/DR) environment (20–25%)
Q: DP-300 vs DP-900 — which should I take first?
A: DP-900 first if databases aren't already your day job. DP-900 teaches the data vocabulary — relational vs non-relational, OLTP vs OLAP — without expecting T-SQL. DP-300 is the role-based Associate exam: it expects you to run Azure SQL workloads in production.
Q: Auto-failover group or active geo-replication — which does DP-300 want?
A: Pick an auto-failover group when the requirement is automatic, transparent failover behind a stable listener endpoint. Pick active geo-replication when the requirement is manual control over failover timing, or more secondaries than a failover group allows. Naming the wrong one for a stated recovery-time requirement is one of the exam's most repeated misses.
Q: What format does the DP-300 exam use?
A: 40–60 questions, with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a real slice of scenario-based, drag-to-match, and multi-select questions, and a smaller mix of dropdown-select, yes/no, and hotspot items. T-SQL snippets and config JSON appear throughout.
Q: What's the DP-300 exam fee, and does renewal cost extra?
A: The voucher is USD $165 in the United States, or around £128 in the UK. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions around events like Build or Ignite, so check your Learn profile before booking. Renewal itself is free, but it happens every year.
Q: Is a DP-300 pass permanent, or does it lapse?
A: It lapses unless renewed. Associate certifications including DP-300 expire annually; renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six months before expiry. Fundamentals certs such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire at all.
Q: Query Store or Extended Events — which does DP-300 expect for troubleshooting?
A: Query Store answers a regression over time — a query that used to run fast and now doesn't. Extended Events answers a live, event-level symptom, such as a deadlock, right now. DP-300 names the symptom, not the tool, so matching the two is the real skill.
Q: DP-300 vs AI-300 — different data roles?
A: They cover different parts of the data stack. DP-300 is for administering Azure SQL workloads in production. AI-300 is for MLOps and GenAIOps across Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on the role you're in.
Q: I need to resit DP-300 — how soon can I book again?
A: Every attempt is a separate booking, and how long you wait depends on which attempt it is. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-300 bank before paying?
A: Yes — the app is free to download, with a free allowance of DP-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 405 DP-300 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does DP-300 revision still work with no connection?
A: Yes. The whole loop stays on-device: practice, scoring, and the readiness read. A missing signal doesn't stop a session, and no account is required. Your study data stays local unless you switch on optional private iCloud sync.

## /exams/dp-700/ — DP-700 Practice Questions — 336 Qs for Fabric Engineer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Implement and manage an analytics solution (30–35%)
  - Ingest and transform data (30–35%)
  - Monitor and optimize an analytics solution (30–35%)
Q: DP-700 vs DP-600 — which should I take?
A: Both are Fabric associate certifications, and your role decides. DP-600 (Analytics Engineer) leans toward semantic models, Power BI, and DAX. DP-700 (Data Engineer) leans toward ingestion and transformation — pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks, PySpark, Eventstream, and KQL. Build the pipelines, take DP-700; model and serve the data, take DP-600.
Q: OneLake shortcut or mirroring — how does DP-700 test the choice?
A: A shortcut references data in place — no copy, no ongoing compute cost — for reading data another workspace already owns. Mirroring actually replicates the source into Fabric's Delta format, near-real time, for when engines need to query it directly. DP-700 names the access pattern, not the mechanism, so inferring it is the real skill.
Q: What question formats appear on DP-700?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank runs a similar mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a meaningful mix of scenario-based and multi-select questions, and a smaller set of yes/no, dropdown, hotspot, drag-to-match, and ordering items, plus a handful of case studies.
Q: What's the DP-700 voucher price?
A: The DP-700 voucher is USD $165 in the United States — associate-level pricing. Cost varies by region; in the UK it's typically around £113. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Learn profile before booking.
Q: Once earned, does DP-700 need renewing?
A: Yes. DP-700 earns the Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate certifications it needs renewing every year. Renewal is free: a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before expiry. Fundamentals certs such as DP-900 never expire.
Q: Dataflow Gen2 or a Data pipeline — which does DP-700 expect for a given ingestion task?
A: Dataflow Gen2 is the low-code, Power Query choice for transformation-heavy loads. A Data pipeline is the orchestration choice for scheduling and chaining activities across sources. DP-700 scenarios describe the requirement, transform-in-place or orchestrate-and-schedule, rather than naming the tool, so spotting which one it implies is the real skill.
Q: Is DP-700 a technical, hands-on exam?
A: Yes. DP-700 expects real data-engineering work in Fabric: writing T-SQL, PySpark, and KQL; designing load patterns; working with Delta tables, shortcuts, mirroring, and pipelines; and optimising Lakehouse and Spark performance. It's a working engineer's exam, not a conceptual overview. Try DP-900 first for a vocabulary-level on-ramp.
Q: I failed DP-700 — how long until I can retake it?
A: Each retake needs a fresh voucher, and the wait grows with every attempt. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's DP-700 bank before paying?
A: Yes — the app is free to download, with a free allowance of DP-700 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 336 DP-700 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does DP-700 practice hold up without a connection?
A: Yes. The app doesn't need a connection for question practice, scoring, or the readiness prediction — all of that runs on-device. No account is required, and your data stays on your device unless you switch on optional iCloud sync.

Q: Liquid clustering or partitioning — which does DP-750 expect for a Delta table?
A: Liquid clustering is the current recommendation when query patterns change over time or cardinality is high; it re-clusters incrementally without a full rewrite. Partitioning still suits low-cardinality columns with stable filters. DP-750 describes the query pattern, not the strategy name, so inferring the right approach is the real skill.
Q: DP-750 vs DP-800 — different data engineering roles?

DP-750 (Databricks Data Engineer) builds production pipelines on Azure Databricks — Unity Catalog, Lakeflow, Delta tables, Spark tuning.
