A: Yes. DP-750 earns the Azure Databricks Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate certifications it needs renewing every year. Renewal is free: a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before expiry. Fundamentals certs such as DP-900 never expire.
Q: Lakeflow Job or Declarative Pipeline — how does DP-750 tell them apart?
A: A Lakeflow Job orchestrates arbitrary tasks, notebooks, SQL, other jobs, on a schedule or trigger, useful when the work isn't purely a transform flow. A Declarative Pipeline expresses a transform graph with dependency management and data-quality expectations built in. Confusing the two is a recurring DP-750 miss.

  - Design and develop database solutions (35–40%)
  - Secure, optimize, and deploy database solutions (35–40%)
  - Implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%)
Q: DP-800 vs DP-300 — which should I take?
A: Different jobs. DP-300 (Database Administrator Associate) runs, secures, tunes, and recovers Azure SQL workloads — HA/DR, performance, automation. DP-800 is for SQL developers bringing AI primitives, embeddings, vector search, RAG, into the data tier through T-SQL. DP-300 administers; DP-800 develops. Many SQL pros take both.
Q: Dynamic Data Masking or Always Encrypted — which does DP-800 want for a given scenario?
A: Dynamic Data Masking hides column values from ordinary users at query time, but a DBA can still see plaintext. Always Encrypted keeps data encrypted client-side, so even a DBA with full access cannot read it. Masking suits ordinary users; Always Encrypted suits protecting data from privileged insiders.
Q: What question formats appear on DP-800?
A: Microsoft's own guidance states 40–60 questions with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank runs a similar mix: mostly single-answer multiple choice, a real slice of drag-to-match and dropdown-select items, and a smaller mix of yes/no, drag-and-drop, and hotspot questions.

A: It needs renewing. Associate certifications including DP-800 expire annually; renewal is a free online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six months before expiry. Fundamentals certs such as DP-900 are different — those don't expire at all.
Q: Vector index or full-text index — how does DP-800 test the choice?
A: A vector index suits semantic retrieval, finding rows whose embeddings are close even when the wording differs. A full-text index suits keyword and phrase matching where exact terms matter. DP-800 checks whether you can name the single index type a stated requirement calls for.
Q: DP-800 vs PL-300 — different data roles?
A: They sit on opposite ends of the data stack. DP-800 brings AI primitives, embeddings, vector search, RAG, into the data tier through T-SQL. PL-300 (Power BI Data Analyst) models and publishes data with Power BI and DAX. Choose based on whether your role writes the data layer or reports on it.

Q: Does the GH-300 GitHub Copilot certification expire?

Q: Who is the GH-300 GitHub Copilot exam for?
A: GH-300 is an intermediate credential for developers who already use Copilot day to day and want to prove applied expertise. It assumes GitHub fundamentals and one programming language. Q: How much of GH-300 is prompt engineering?
A: Prompt engineering and context crafting is its own domain, weighted 10–15%. Q: GH-300 vs AZ-400 — is there any overlap for a DevOps engineer?
A: Some, but different layers. AZ-400 covers pipelines, releases, and security across Azure DevOps and GitHub at a platform-engineering level. GH-300 stays focused on Copilot itself: using it responsibly, prompting it well, and configuring privacy controls. Neither substitutes for the other.

  - Apply Modern Development Practices (10–15%)
  - Manage Projects with GitHub (5–10%)
  - Understand Privacy, Security, and Administration (10–15%)
  - Explore the GitHub Community (5–10%)
Q: How much does the GH-900 exam cost?
A: The GitHub Foundations exam is USD $99, a price set by GitHub rather than Microsoft's standard certification pricing. GH-900 is delivered through Microsoft's exam platform, but the certification itself is owned and maintained by GitHub.
Q: Does the GH-900 GitHub Foundations certification expire?
A: Yes. Unlike Microsoft's own Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900, which never expire, GitHub Foundations is valid for two years from the date you pass. To stay certified, you re-sit GH-900 — GitHub sets this two-year validity, not Microsoft.
Q: What is the GH-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: GH-900 follows the standard Microsoft exam-delivery retake policy even though GitHub owns the credential. First retake: after 24 hours. Second, third, fourth, and fifth retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts in any rolling 12-month period, each needing a fresh booking.
Q: GH-900 vs AZ-900 — what's the difference?
A: GH-900 validates collaboration on GitHub: Git, repositories, pull requests, Actions, and the open-source community. AZ-900 validates cloud concepts and core Azure services. They're independent credentials in different product families, and DevOps-minded candidates often earn both.
Q: What should I expect from GH-900's exam format?
A: GitHub gives candidates 100 minutes and says the question count can vary. Azure Master's original practice bank weights single-answer and scenario items most heavily, with multi-select, drag-to-match, and hotspot questions included for broader interaction practice.
Q: Is GH-900 worth taking if I'm not a developer?
A: Yes — GH-900 is explicitly designed for non-developers as well as developers. Project managers, technical writers, and product owners all sit it to prove they can collaborate effectively on GitHub. It doesn't ask you to write code, just to explain how the platform's features fit together.
Q: GH-900 vs GH-300 — foundations or the Copilot-specific exam?
A: GH-300 narrows in on one tool: using Copilot responsibly, prompting it well, and administering it at scale. GH-900 is the broad on-ramp with no assumed Copilot depth. Non-developers usually stop at GH-900; developers proving Copilot fluency move on to GH-300.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's GH-900 content before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download, with a free allowance of GH-900 questions to try every feature first. The full bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does GH-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes — GH-900 practice runs its questions, scoring, and readiness prediction entirely on-device, so a commute or flight with no connection doesn't interrupt your revision. No account is needed, and data stays on your device unless you enable iCloud sync.

## /exams/pl-300/ — PL-300 Practice Questions — 378 Qs for Power BI Analyst (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Prepare the data (25–30%)
  - Model the data (25–30%)
  - Visualize and analyze the data (25–30%)
  - Manage and secure Power BI (15–20%)
Q: PL-300 vs DP-900 — which should I take first?
A: Take DP-900 first if relational vs non-relational data, transactional vs analytical workloads, or Azure's SQL family aren't familiar yet. PL-300 assumes you already know the difference when it asks about DirectLake vs DirectQuery vs Import or Fabric semantic models. Skip DP-900 if you already do analyst work day-to-day.
Q: PL-300 vs DP-300 — different roles?
A: Different angles on the data stack. PL-300 is the analyst-side cert: Power Query M, DAX, visualisations, governance and sharing. DP-300 is the operational DBA cert: HA/DR, performance tuning, security, and automation for Azure SQL. Larger teams often split the two roles.
Q: Are there formal prerequisites for PL-300?
A: No mandatory prior exam, but Microsoft's audience profile expects proficiency with Power Query and DAX, plus comfort working with stakeholders on requirements and with data engineers on sourcing. Candidates without hands-on Power BI experience usually need a longer run-up, even though nothing blocks booking directly.
Q: What's the PL-300 exam format like?
A: PL-300 sits in Microsoft's 40–60 question Associate band, with formats varying by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank weights single-answer and dropdown-select items heaviest, reflecting how often the exam asks you to predict a DAX result or Power Query step, alongside multi-select, drag-to-match, and case-study questions.
Q: Does PL-300 prep need a live internet connection?
A: No. Every part of PL-300 practice, including the Exam IQ prediction, runs on your device rather than a server, so full sessions work on a delayed train or a long-haul flight. No account is needed, and data stays put unless you opt into private iCloud sync.
Q: Can I test-drive Azure Mastery's PL-300 content for free?
A: Yes. The app is free to download, with a free allowance of PL-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 378 PL-300 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or unlock every exam with a subscription or lifetime upgrade.
Q: If I don't pass PL-300, when can I try again?
A: Not immediately, and each attempt needs its own voucher. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: Will my PL-300 badge lapse if I don't renew?
A: Yes. Associate certifications including PL-300 expire annually. Renewal is a free, short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within six months of your expiry date. Fundamentals certs like AZ-900 are different — those never expire.
Q: What's the going rate for a PL-300 exam attempt?
A: The PL-300 voucher is USD $165 in the US, or around £128 in the UK — pricing varies by region. Microsoft occasionally runs free-voucher promotions around events like Build or Ignite, so check your Learn profile first.

Q: Canvas app or model-driven app — how does PL-900 test the difference?

Q: I didn't pass first time — when can I book a PL-900 resit?

Q: Is PL-900 worth taking if I'm not a developer?
A: Yes. PL-900 is built for a mixed audience: business analysts, citizen developers, project managers, and IT pros sizing up low-code all sit it. You're not asked to write code, just to pick the right app or flow type for a scenario, a sensible first stop before building for real.

## /exams/retired/ — Retired Microsoft Exams & Successors | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-09-04
Q: Can I still book a retired exam?
A: No. Once Microsoft retires an exam, Pearson VUE stops scheduling new sittings for it — that now includes AZ-500, the last of the five on this page to close, on 31 August 2026.
Q: Does my credential expire when the exam retires?
A: No. A credential you earned by passing a Microsoft exam stays valid and stays on your Microsoft Learn transcript after the exam itself retires — retirement stops new bookings, it doesn't undo a credential you've already earned.
Q: Can I renew a credential from a retired exam?
A: No. When Microsoft retires an exam, its renewal assessment retires with it, so the credential cannot be renewed after the retirement date. It stays on your transcript as earned. To hold a current credential in that area, sit the successor exam listed above.
Q: Do retired questions still count in the app?
A: Azure Mastery keeps each retired exam's question bank in the app as reference material for anyone who bought it, or passed the exam before it retired. It isn't counted in the app's advertised exam or question totals.
Q: Which retired exam maps to which successor?
A: AI-900 to AI-901, AI-102 to AI-103, DP-100 to AI-300, AZ-204 to AI-200, and AZ-500 to SC-500. The table above lists each one with its retirement date.

## /exams/sc-100/ — SC-100 Practice Questions — 452 Qs for Cyber Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities (20–25%)
  - Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for applications and data (20–25%)
Q: MCRA vs MCSB — which framework does a given SC-100 scenario want?
A: MCRA shows how security capabilities fit together, while MCSB provides prescriptive security recommendations. A posture-management tool can assess an environment against MCSB, but the benchmark itself is guidance rather than a measurement service.
Q: What's the SC-100 prerequisite?
A: You can sit SC-100 with no prior certification. To earn the Cybersecurity Architect Expert credential, you must also hold an active SC-200, SC-300, or SC-500 Associate certification. Microsoft replaced the retired AZ-500 route with SC-500 in the current prerequisite list. An exam pass alone is not the prerequisite; the Associate credential must be active on your profile.
Q: What format does the SC-100 exam use?
A: 40–60 questions, with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer, a meaningful share of scenario questions, yes/no and multi-select in roughly equal measure, plus a smaller mix of drag-to-match, dropdown, hotspot, ordering, and case-study items.
Q: What's the SC-100 exam fee, and does renewal add to the cost?
A: The voucher costs USD $165 in the United States, around £128 in the UK. Microsoft occasionally runs free-voucher promotions around events like Build or Ignite. Renewal itself is free, a short annual online assessment, so factor only the original voucher into long-term cost.
Q: Is SC-100 a lifetime certification, or does it need renewing?
A: The Cybersecurity Architect Expert credential is valid for one year. In the final six months, renew it at no charge through Microsoft's current online assessment; its length can change as the skills outline evolves. Fundamentals credentials such as AZ-900 do not expire.
Q: SC-100 vs AZ-305 — which next for an architect?
A: Different lenses. SC-100 is the security architect cert: Zero Trust, ransomware resilience, SecOps strategy, identity governance. AZ-305 is the solutions architect cert: data, infrastructure, business continuity, identity and monitoring. They overlap on identity and governance; many senior architects hold both.
Q: How soon can I resit SC-100 after a fail?
A: A first retake is available after 24 hours. First retake: 24-hour wait. Second and third retakes: 14-day wait each. Five attempts maximum per rolling 12 months, a fresh voucher required each sitting.
Q: How is SC-100 different from an Associate-level security exam?
A: Associate exams like SC-200 and SC-300 test configuring a named product correctly. SC-100 tests designing the strategy those products serve, choosing between Sentinel automation and Defender XDR-native response for stated constraints. Multiple options can be valid; only one best satisfies the scenario.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-100 bank before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download with a free allowance of SC-100 questions so you can try every feature. The full 452-question bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Can I rehearse SC-100 scenarios with no internet connection?
A: Yes. Practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, working with no connection at all. No account is required, and iCloud sync stays optional and private if you want it.

## /exams/sc-200/ — SC-200 Practice Questions — 374 Qs for SOC Analyst (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06

  - Manage a security operations environment (40–45%)
  - Respond to security incidents (35–40%)
  - Perform threat hunting (20–25%)
Q: Do I need to know KQL before starting SC-200?
A: Not on day one, but learn it early: threat hunting is 20–25% of the exam and KQL shows up in the other domains too. Start by reading and modifying existing queries before writing from scratch; the exam tests picking the right table and interpreting results more than raw syntax.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first if security concepts are new to you: it builds the cross-cutting vocabulary without expecting hands-on triage. SC-200 is the role-based Associate exam, investigating incidents in Defender XDR and writing KQL hunting queries. Most candidates pass SC-900 in weeks, then spend two to three months on SC-200.
Q: What question formats show up on SC-200?
A: 40–60 questions, with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank mirrors that mix: mostly single-answer, a meaningful share of scenario and multi-select questions in roughly equal measure, a smaller set of yes/no, dropdown, hotspot, and drag-to-match items, and a handful of case studies.
Q: What's the SC-200 voucher price, and is renewal extra?
A: SC-200's voucher runs USD $165 in the United States, roughly £128 in the UK, with Microsoft occasionally offering free vouchers around Build or Ignite. Renewal itself costs nothing beyond a short annual assessment, so the voucher is the only real ongoing expense.
Q: Does an SC-200 pass last forever, or do I need to renew?
A: No, it needs renewing. Associate certifications including SC-200 expire annually; renewal is a free, short online assessment within six months of expiry, targeting recent outline updates. Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 differ: those never expire.
Q: Sentinel automation or Defender XDR native response — how does SC-200 test the choice?
A: SC-200 scenarios give you an incident that could plausibly be handled either way, and expect you to pick based on where the signal originates and how broad the response needs to be, not personal preference. Answer Coach spells out which property of the scenario should have driven the call.
Q: I need to retake SC-200 — what's the wait?
A: 24 hours covers the wait before your first retake. First retake: 24-hour wait. Second and third retakes: 14-day wait each. Microsoft limits you to five attempts in any rolling 12-month window, a new voucher required each time.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-200 bank before paying?

Q: Can I hunt through SC-200 practice scenarios with no connection?
A: Yes. Practice sessions, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so they work with no connection at all. There's no account to sign into, and data stays local unless you turn on optional, private iCloud sync.

## /exams/sc-300/ — SC-300 Practice Questions — 428 Qs for Identity Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Implement and manage user identities (20–25%)
  - Implement authentication and access management (25–30%)
  - Plan and implement workload identities (20–25%)
  - Plan and automate identity governance (20–25%)
Q: PIM eligible vs active assignment — how does SC-300 test the difference?
A: Scenarios describe a user needing a privileged role only occasionally, then ask whether eligible or active Privileged Identity Management fits: eligible needs just-in-time activation and approval, active is already usable without that step. Answer Coach names exactly which requirement in the scenario should have decided it.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-100 — which next for an identity specialist?
A: Pass SC-300 first. SC-300 is Associate-level and operational: configure and run Entra ID, Conditional Access, and identity governance day-to-day. SC-100 is Expert-level and architectural, designing the Zero Trust strategy those controls implement. SC-300 is also one of three accepted routes to the SC-100 credential.
Q: What format does the SC-300 exam use?
A: 40–60 questions, with formats that vary by sitting. Azure Mastery's bank runs a similar spread: mostly single-answer, a substantial share of yes/no and multi-select questions, a meaningful set of scenario items, and a smaller mix of dropdown, drag-to-match, hotspot, ordering, and case-study formats.
Q: What's the SC-300 exam fee, and is renewal on top?
A: The SC-300 voucher is USD $165 in the United States, roughly £128 in the UK. Microsoft occasionally offers free vouchers around events like Build or Ignite. Renewal is free too, a short annual assessment, so budget for the voucher only, not a recurring fee.
Q: Does an SC-300 pass need renewing each year?
A: SC-300's Associate credential is annual. When its last six months begin, your Learn profile offers a free online renewal focused on the current identity-and-access outline; the assessment has no guaranteed fixed question count. By contrast, Fundamentals credentials such as AZ-900 do not expire.
Q: Pass-through Authentication or Password Hash Sync — which does SC-300 want?
A: The deciding factor is resilience. PHS keeps authenticating during an on-premises outage since Entra ID holds a password hash; PTA validates against on-premises AD in real time and fails if that link drops, but keeps passwords entirely on-premises. Outage-tolerance scenarios want PHS; strict on-premises-only policies want PTA.
Q: I need to resit SC-300 — how long before I can rebook?
A: Retake number one is available 24 hours after a fail. First retake: 24-hour wait. Second and third retakes: 14-day wait each. Five attempts is the ceiling per rolling 12 months, each needing its own voucher.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first if security and identity concepts are new to you: it builds the cross-cutting vocabulary without expecting hands-on Conditional Access or PIM work. SC-300 is the role-based Associate exam, operating Entra ID at scale day-to-day. Most candidates pass SC-900 in weeks, then spend months on SC-300.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-300 bank before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download with a free allowance of SC-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full 428-question bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Can I revise SC-300 with no data connection?
A: Yes, no connection needed. Practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction are all on-device, so a commute or a flight works fine for study. No account is required, and iCloud sync stays optional and private.

Exam domains:
  - Manage identity, access, and governance (20–25%)
  - Secure storage, databases, and networking (25–30%)
  - Secure compute (20–25%)
  - Manage and monitor security posture (20–25%)
Q: Is SC-500 replacing AZ-500?
A: Yes. SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer) is the direct successor to AZ-500, which retired on 31 August 2026. It keeps AZ-500's core security-engineering content and adds securing cloud and AI workloads: Copilot, Entra Agent ID, Foundry, and Defender for AI. If you haven't started AZ-500, prepare for SC-500 instead.
Q: How much does the SC-500 exam cost?
A: The SC-500 voucher is USD $165 in the United States, around £128 in the UK; regional pricing varies. Watch for free-voucher promotions around Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite. Renewal is free, but it's an annual Associate certification, so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-500 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-500 expire annually. Renewal is a free, short assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six-month window before expiry. Fundamentals certifications like SC-900 don't expire.
Q: What is the SC-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: Each retake takes longer than the last, and every attempt requires its own voucher purchase. First retake: after 24 hours. Second and third retakes: a 14-day wait each. Cap: five attempts per rolling 12 months.
Q: How long should I study for SC-500?
A: Most candidates pass after four to eight weeks with some prior Azure and Entra experience; plan two to three months if cloud security is genuinely new. The exam expects hands-on knowledge of Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Entra ID, and Key Vault. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're actually ready.
Q: What prior experience does SC-500 assume?
A: SC-500 assumes hands-on Azure and hybrid administration — compute, network, storage — plus strong Entra ID familiarity. It isn't a from-scratch security course: you're expected to already operate the infrastructure you're securing. New to Azure administration? Work through AZ-104 or the free AZ-900 first.
Q: SC-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. SC-500 covers implementing security controls across identity, storage, networking, compute, and AI workloads. SC-200 covers running Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, focused on detection and incident response. Many Cybersecurity Architect candidates hold both.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-500 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 432 SC-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-500 practice work offline?
A: Yes — every question, score, and readiness read happens on-device, so SC-500 prep keeps going without a connection. No account is needed, and nothing leaves your device unless you switch on private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-500 practice test mode?
A: Yes. Timed practice sessions draw on original, blueprint-weighted SC-500 questions with published timing and the interactive formats this exam uses. Adaptive study and Focus Weak Spots then push you back toward the domains dragging your accuracy down.

## /exams/sc-900/ — SC-900 Practice Questions — 397 Qs for Security Basics (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-09-06
Exam domains:
  - Describe the concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra (25–30%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (35–40%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (20–25%)
Q: Which Defender product owns which surface — does SC-900 test that?
A: Yes, repeatedly. SC-900 expects you to place Defender for Endpoint, Cloud Apps, Identity, Office 365, and Cloud against the surface each one actually protects rather than by product name alone. Answer Coach names the specific surface a wrong pick would have left uncovered.
Q: SC-900 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: Pick based on which vocabulary you need first. SC-900 teaches Microsoft's security, identity, and compliance stack; AZ-900 teaches general Azure fundamentals like regions, compute, and pricing. Security-adjacent roles start with SC-900; newcomers to Azure generally start with AZ-900. Many candidates sit both.
Q: What question formats come up on SC-900?
A: SC-900's assessed time is 45 minutes. Microsoft does not promise an exact format in advance, but says most Fundamentals exams contain 35–50 questions. Azure Master's original security-fundamentals bank uses single-select, scenario, multi-select, drag-to-match, hot-area, dropdown, case-study, and drag-and-drop practice.
Q: What's the SC-900 exam fee, and does it vary by region?
A: The SC-900 voucher costs USD $99 in the United States, and pricing varies by region, around £77 in the UK. Microsoft occasionally runs free-voucher promotions around events like Build or Ignite, so check your Learn profile before booking.
Q: Once passed, does an SC-900 certification lapse?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications, including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, SC-900, and PL-900, never expire once you pass. Associate and Expert certifications such as SC-200 or SC-300 differ: those need an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.
Q: Purview compliance solutions — what's the recurring SC-900 trap?
A: Candidates reach for the Purview tool they've heard of, not the one built for the stated requirement, confusing a DLP policy with a sensitivity label, or a retention policy with an eDiscovery case. Answer Coach spells out that distinction whenever you miss one.
Q: I need to resit SC-900 — how long is the wait?
A: The wait before your first retake is 24 hours. First retake: 24-hour wait. Second and third retakes: 14-day wait each. Five attempts maximum per rolling 12 months, each needing a new voucher.
Q: Is SC-900 worth taking if I'm not technical?
A: Yes. SC-900 targets a broad audience on purpose: business stakeholders weighing security procurement, IT generalists working near security, and students entering the field all sit it. You won't configure Conditional Access or write KQL, just pick which Defender product covers a described surface.
Q: Can I try Azure Mastery's SC-900 bank before paying?
A: Yes. The app is free to download with a free allowance of SC-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full 397-question bank unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or a subscription unlocks every exam in the catalogue.
Q: Does SC-900 revision work with no signal?
A: Yes. Practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device rather than through a server, so a train tunnel or aeroplane mode works fine. No account is needed, and iCloud sync stays optional and private.
